part.text: [{"type": "contradiction", "quote": "| Budget-sensitive bounded coding or repository sweeps | Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol at `medium` | Sonnet 5.5 at `medium` or `high`; GLM-5.3 Flash at `max`; Opus 5.5 at `low` |", "scenario": "Caller states a cost limit for a bounded 3-file bugfix. Sol and Sonnet are unavailable so fallback reaches Opus 5.5 at `low`.", "policy_answer": "Fallback orders Opus 5.5 at `low` for bounded coding, but fleet says Use `low` only for trivial, readily checked tasks.", "fix": "Change the budget fallback to Opus 5.5 at `medium` or restrict `low` to trivial checks."}, {"type": "contradiction", "quote": "| Difficult implementation, refactoring, debugging, or test construction | Claude with Opus 5.5 | Sonnet 5.5 at `xhigh`; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol at `xhigh` |", "scenario": "Difficult refactoring lane needs a worker. Opus 5.5 is unavailable so first fallback is Sonnet 5.5 at `xhigh`.", "policy_answer": "Lane orders Sonnet 5.5 at `xhigh` first. Sonnet notes say Above `high`, it costs about as much as Opus 5.5 at lower quality, so prefer Opus 5.5.", "fix": "Remove Sonnet 5.5 at `xhigh` fallback or limit Sonnet fallback to `high`."}, {"type": "contradiction", "quote": "Review GPT-6.1 Sol, Astra, Luna, or Daybreak work with Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, or Grok 4.7.", "scenario": "GPT-6.1 Sol finishes difficult implementation. Orchestrator picks Grok 4.7 as the sole reviewer.", "policy_answer": "Pairing allows Grok 4.7 as reviewer. Fleet lists Grok 4.7 among weaker models and says Treat their findings as leads, not verdicts.", "fix": "Restrict Grok 4.7 to extra challenger and require Opus/Sonnet/Fable/Astra for the verdict."}, {"type": "unsafe", "quote": "| Security review, authorized vulnerability exploration, or patch validation | Codex with Daybreak Blue | GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol; Opus 5.5 for defensive review of the caller's own code; GLM-5.3 for text-only input |", "scenario": "Caller authorizes vulnerability exploration on its own repo. Daybreak, Astra, and Sol are unavailable so fallback reaches Opus 5.5.", "policy_answer": "Fallback allows Opus 5.5. Opus notes say Cyber safeguards send most security work to Opus 4.8, which is outside this fleet.", "fix": "Limit security fallback to in-fleet models that retain the lane or mark the lane Unrouted."}, {"type": "gap", "quote": "| OpenCode | Set by the lane table | Set by the lane table | Open-weight, multimodal, and low-cost lanes |", "scenario": "Caller pins worker CLI to OpenCode for ambiguous planning. Planning row lists only Claude, Fable, Astra, and Sol.", "policy_answer": "Default is Set by the lane table. No planning row lists an OpenCode route, so no explicit route or effort exists.", "fix": "Define an explicit OpenCode default route and effort or mark pinned planning lanes Unrouted."}, {"type": "ambiguity", "quote": "| Ambiguous planning, architecture, orchestration, or synthesis | Claude with Opus 5.5 | Fable 5.1; GPT-6 Astra; GPT-6.1 Sol |", "scenario": "Ambiguous architecture lane routes to Claude with Opus 5.5. Row lists no effort value.", "policy_answer": "Row gives no effort, but skill requires explicit effort. Both high and xhigh rules cover synthesis with no priority.", "fix": "Add explicit effort to every lane-table route or define precedence between default high and xhigh."}, {"type": "contradiction", "quote": "If no supported effort meets the task requirement, advance through the provider list before changing models.", "scenario": "Multimodal lane selects meta contributor identifier. It lacks `max` while next model fallback is Opus 5.5.", "policy_answer": "Muse rule says advance through provider list. Launch rule says If none fits, try the next fallback to a different model.", "fix": "Define that provider-list exhaustion precedes model fallback and update the route card Fallback field accordingly."}, {"type": "unsafe", "quote": "Use only Muse Spark 1.3 for Muse routes. Prefer contributor routes after explicit acceptance of their data terms.", "scenario": "Multimodal lane can use free contributor route. Orchestrator has no record of caller accepting data terms.", "policy_answer": "Policy requires explicit acceptance then skip when terms are not accepted. It defines no owner, check, or record for acceptance.", "fix": "Require recorded caller acceptance in the lane contract before selecting any contributor identifier."}, {"type": "gap", "quote": "Keep a session that Kimi K3 started on Kimi K3, because a model switch loses that history.", "scenario": "Second-opinion lane starts on Grok 4.7. It fails then falls back to Kimi K3 in the same lane.", "policy_answer": "Policy allows Kimi K3 when the harness preserves full history. It also says Start each new lane in a fresh session with no defined history-preservation check.", "fix": "Specify fresh-session fallback procedure and a pre-launch harness history check for Kimi K3."}, {"type": "contradiction", "quote": "Use `max` when the caller requires one worker or a fixed delegation structure.", "scenario": "Caller requires one worker for bounded sweep. Lane falls back to Sonnet 5.5 at `medium`.", "policy_answer": "One-worker rule demands `max`. Bounded fallback specifies Sonnet 5.5 at `medium` and Sonnet notes say Avoid `max`; it produces very high output-token counts.", "fix": "Scope the one-worker max rule to models whose range allows max and let explicit fallback effort win."}]
